p: וַיְחִי יַעֲקֹב בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם שְׁבַע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וַיְהִי יְמֵי יַעֲקֹב וְגוֹמֵר וַיִּקְרְבוּ יְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לָמוּת.
— Jacob lived in the land of Egypt for seventeen years, and the days of Jacob were, and so forth; and the days of Israel drew near to die.

לְהָבִין זֹאת מַה דְּאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (ריו ב) וּבְתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ (סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פֶּרֶק ה) שֶׁי״ז שָׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁבְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם הָיָה עִיקַּר הַחַיִּים שֶׁלּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בְּצַעַר וְשֶׁלֹּא בְּיֵצֶר הָרָע וּמֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא.

— We must understand the teaching of the holy Zohar (216b) and Tanna Devei Eliyahu (Seder Eliyahu Rabbah, chapter 5): these seventeen years in Egypt constituted his principal life, free of suffering and of the evil inclination, resembling the World to Come.

וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נֶאֱמַר בִּלְשׁוֹן יַעֲקֹב שֶׁהוּא קַטְנוּת הַמַּדְרֵגָה כַּיָּדוּעַ וּכְמוֹ כֵן בִּכְלָלוּת חַיָּיו קמ״ז שָׁנָה נֶאֱמַר גַּם כֵּן בְּשֵׁם יַעֲקֹב וְאַחַר כָּךְ נֶאֱמַר בִּלְשׁוֹן וַיִּקְרְבוּ יְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹמֵר שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַמַּדְרֵגָה הַגְּדוֹלָה.

— Nevertheless, Scripture uses the name Jacob, which, as is known, denotes a lesser spiritual level. Likewise, when totaling his one hundred and forty-seven years, it again uses Jacob; afterward it says, “The days of Israel drew near,” and so forth, denoting the higher level.
וְהִקְשָׁה זֶה גַּם כֵּן בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (רכא ב).
— The holy Zohar (221b) likewise raises this difficulty.
וְגַם הֲלֹא אָמְרוּ (סוֹף פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּבָבָא בַּתְרָא) שֶׁשְּׁלֹשֶׁת הָאָבוֹת הִטְעִימָן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מֵעֵין הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא וְלֹא שָׁלַט בָּהֶן יֵצֶר הָרָע

— Moreover, the Sages said (at the end of the first chapter of Bava Batra) that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave the three patriarchs a taste of the World to Come in this world, and the evil inclination did not rule over them;
וְדָרְשׁוּ מִדִּכְתִיב בַּכֹּל מִכֹּל כֹּל
— they derived this from the expressions “with everything,” “of everything,” and “everything.”
וְהִנֵּה זֶה שֶׁאָמַר יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְכִי יֶשׁ לִי כֹל הָיָה עוֹד הַרְבֵּה שָׁנִים קוֹדֶם וַיְחִי יַעֲקֹב בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם
— Jacob’s declaration, “For I have everything,” occurred many years before “Jacob lived in the land of Egypt.”
וְאָז כְּבָר נִשְׁלַם בִּבְחִינַת כֹּל הַיְינוּ שְׁלֵימוּת הַחַיִּים
— He had already attained the aspect of “everything,” meaning perfected life.
וְהֵיאַךְ אָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ וּבְתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ שֶׁעִיקַּר שְׁלֵימוּת הַחַיִּים הָיָה הַשְּׁבַע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וּבְאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם דַּיְיקָא.
— How, then, did the holy Zohar and Tanna Devei Eliyahu say that life’s principal perfection occurred during those seventeen years, specifically in Egypt?

paragraphs.text: Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 5: “Why did Jacob merit life in this world without suffering and without the evil inclination, like what the Holy One, blessed be He, will give the righteous in the future? Because he sat in the house of study from youth to old age, proficient in Scripture, Mishnah, laws, and aggadot, as it says, “Jacob was a wholehearted man, dwelling in tents”; also, “Like arrows in a warrior’s hand are the sons of youth; fortunate is the man…”; and, “To whom shall he teach knowledge?… Those weaned from milk, withdrawn from the breast.” When he left his father’s house for Laban’s, the Divine Presence stood above him and answered: Jacob My son, raise your eyes to heaven. See the twelve constellations and the stars in the firmament, the twelve hours of day and twelve hours of night, corresponding to the twelve tribes I give you. When Jacob returned from Laban’s house and Joseph was sold, he wept and mourned twenty-two years, as it says, “All his sons and daughters arose to comfort him… His father wept for him.” Was he weeping only for Joseph? Rather, he said: Perhaps I incurred guilt by marrying two sisters, or by benefiting from Laban’s or Shechem’s wealth, and the covenant the Holy One, blessed be He, made with me has been annulled. Immediately the mercy of the Holy One, blessed be He, was stirred, and He gave Jacob seventeen good years near his old age, resembling the world to come. From here they said: Whoever experiences one good year near old age has a favorable sign; whoever experiences one bad year near old age has an unfavorable sign. Our father Jacob enjoyed goodness during the seventeen years he was in Egypt, and the Holy One, blessed be He, accounted it to him as though all his days had been good, as it says: “Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years.””

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 216b: “Here it says, “He lived.” Throughout all his earlier days it had not been called “he lived,” because all his days had been spent in suffering. Of him it is written: “I was not at ease, I was not quiet, I had no rest, and turmoil came.” After he went down to Egypt it says, “He lived.” He saw his son a king; he saw all his sons worthy and righteous, all enjoying the world’s delights and comforts, while he sat among them like good wine resting on its lees. Then it says, “Jacob lived.” There is no separation between “they were fruitful and multiplied greatly” and “Jacob lived,” and so it should be. “Seventeen years”—why seventeen years? Rabbi Shimon said: All Jacob’s days had been spent in suffering. When he saw Joseph standing before him, whenever Jacob looked at Joseph he felt whole within himself, as though he saw Joseph’s mother, for Joseph’s beauty resembled Rachel’s beauty. He felt as though he had never experienced suffering in all his days.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 221b: ““The days of Israel drew near to die.” It was taught: Rabbi Chiyya said: It is written, “Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years.” There, during his life, he is called Jacob; here, at his death, he is called Israel, for it says: “The days of Israel drew near to die.” Rabbi Yosei said: It is indeed so. It does not say “the day of Israel drew near to die,” but “the days.” Does a person die over several days? He dies and departs from the world in a single hour, a single instant. Rather, we learned: When the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to take a person’s spirit back to Himself, all the days that person lived in this world are reviewed before Him and enter the reckoning. When they approach Him for the reckoning, the person dies and the Holy One, blessed be He, takes back the spirit, the breath that He breathed into him. Fortunate is the person whose days approach the King without shame, with not one day rejected because a sin was committed in it. Therefore “drawing near” is said of the righteous: their days approach the King without shame. Woe to the wicked, of whom “drawing near” is not said! How can their days approach the King when all their days were filled with the world’s sins? They do not approach the King, are not counted before Him or remembered above, but perish. Of them it is written: “The way of the wicked is like darkness; they do not know what makes them stumble.” Here, however, “the days of Israel drew near”—without shame, in wholeness and complete joy. Hence “the days of Israel,” for Israel is more complete than Jacob. If you ask: Is it not written “Jacob was a wholehearted man,” meaning complete? He was complete, but not complete in the higher degree of Israel. It was taught: Rabbi Yosei said: When a person’s days are reviewed before the King, there is a righteous person whose days are reviewed yet remain distant from the King, and there is a righteous person whose days are close to the King and never distant. They enter without shame and approach the King. Fortunate is their portion! This is what is written: “The days of Israel drew near to die.””

p: אָמְנָם יוּבַן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא לג:) וּלְבֵית יַעֲקֹב חַטֹּאתָם אֵלּוּ עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוֹת לָהֶם כִּשְׁגָגוֹת.
— This can be understood through the teaching (Bava Metzia 33b), “‘And to the house of Jacob their sins’—these are the unlearned, whose deliberate sins are treated as inadvertent ones.”

כִּי בְּוַדַּאי יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּעֶצֶם שֹׁרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹ כְּבָר הָיָה נִשְׁלַם בְּעֵת שֶׁיָּשַׂר אֶל הַמַּלְאָךְ וַיּוּכַל שֶׁהָיָה שָׂרוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו שֶׁהוּא כֹּחַ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע.

— Certainly our patriarch Jacob, peace be upon him, had already attained perfection in the essential root of his soul when he strove with the angel and prevailed. This was Esau’s ministering angel, the power of the evil inclination.
וְקָרָא שְׁמוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי שָׂרִיתָ עִם אֱלֹהִים וְגוֹמֵר וְלָכֵן אַחַר זֶה אָמַר לְעֵשָׂו וְכִי יֶשׁ לִי כֹל שֶׁכְּבָר זָכָה בֶאֱמֶת לִשְׁלֵימוּת הַחַיּוּת שֶׁלֹּא בְּיֵצֶר הָרָע.

— He called his name Israel, “For you have striven with divine beings,” and so forth. Therefore, afterward he told Esau, “For I have everything,” since he had truly attained perfected vitality free of the evil inclination.

אַךְ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁכָּל עִנְיָנוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לִסְבּוֹל צַעַר גִּידּוּל בָּנִים כְּדֵי לְהַשְׁרִישׁ הַקְּדוּשָּׁה לְזַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו לְדוֹרוֹת עוֹלָם גַּם לַנְּפָשׁוֹת הַנְּמוּכִים אֲשֶׁר בְּשֵׁם יַעֲקֹב יְכוּנֶּה שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ גַּם כֵּן לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁלֹּא בְּיֵצֶר הָרָע.

— Yet Jacob’s entire purpose was to endure the suffering of raising children, thereby rooting holiness within his descendants for all generations—even the lowly souls designated by the name Jacob—so that they too might merit the life of the World to Come, free of the evil inclination.
וְזֶה הָיָה דַּיְיקָא בְּי״ז שָׁנָה שֶׁהָיָה בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם שֶׁאָז נִשְׁלַם הַחַיּוּת גַּם בִּנְפָשׁוֹת שֶׁל בְּחִינַת יַעֲקֹב כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
— This occurred specifically during the seventeen years he spent in Egypt, when vitality was perfected also in souls belonging to the aspect of Jacob, as explained above.

וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לוֹ בְּמַרְאוֹת הַלַּיְלָה יַעֲקֹב יַעֲקֹב אַל תִּירָא מֵרְדָה מִצְרַיְמָה כִּי לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל אֲשִׂימְךָ שָׁם דַּיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי יְרִידָתָם לְמִצְרַיִם יִתְבָּרְרוּ כָּל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת לִהְיוֹתָם מוּכָנִים לְקַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה.

— Thus he was told in the visions of the night, “Jacob, Jacob, do not fear to descend to Egypt, for I will make you a great nation there.” Specifically through their descent to Egypt, all the souls would be refined and prepared to receive the Torah.
שֶׁהֵם בְּעַצְמָם שֶׁזָּכוּ לְהִזְדַּכֵּךְ הָיוּ כָּל הַס׳ רִבּוֹא נְפָשׁוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ הַדּוֹר דֵּעָה.
— Those very souls that merited refinement comprised the entire six hundred thousand souls of the generation of knowledge.

וְזֶה עִנְיַן פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ שֶׁהוּא סוֹף סֵפֶר בְּרֵאשִׁית וַיְחִי יַעֲקֹב בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם י״ז שָׁנָה שֶׁבָּזֶה נִשְׁלַם שְׁלֵימוּת הַבְּרִיאָה גַּם לַנְּפָשׁוֹת הַפְּחוּתִים שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם.

— This is the meaning of this Torah portion, which concludes Genesis: “Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years.” Through this, creation’s perfection was completed even for the lowliest souls of Israel, so that they might merit eternal life.

h: Rabbi and the Suffering of Refinement

p: וְאִיתָא בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה עַל רַבִּי שֶׁהָיָה נִיצוֹץ מִנִּשְׁמַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה דָּר בְּצִיפּוֹרִי י״ז שָׁנָה וְקָרָא עַל עַצְמוֹ וַיְחִי יַעֲקֹב בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם י״ז שָׁנָה וְחָיָה יְהוּדָה וְכוּלֵי.

— Bereishit Rabbah relates concerning Rabbi, who was a spark of our patriarch Jacob’s soul, that he lived in Sepphoris for seventeen years and applied to himself the verse, “Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years”—“Judah lived,” and so forth.
וְכָל אוֹתָם הַשָּׁנִים הָיָה חוֹשֵׁשׁ בְּיִסּוּרִין כְּדֵי לְתַקֵּן כְּלָלוּת נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ לִשְׁלֵימוּת הַחַיּוּת שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַבָּא
— Throughout those years he suffered afflictions in order to rectify the collective souls of Israel, so that they might attain the perfected vitality of the World to Come.
וְגַם מַה שֶּׁעָבַר עֲלֵיהֶם יִהְיֶה בַּסּוֹף נִתְקַן הַכֹּל כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְרַבִּים מִיְּשֵׁנֵי אַדְמַת עָפָר יָקִיצוּ וְגוֹמֵר
— Everything that had befallen them would ultimately be rectified, as it says, “Many of those who sleep in the dusty earth shall awaken,” and so forth.
וְעִנְיַן הַיְקִיצָה נֶאֱמַר בַּצַּדִּיקִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר הָקִיצוּ וְרַנְּנוּ שׁוֹכְנֵי עָפָר שֶׁהַמִּיתָה הוּא רַק כְּשֵׁינָה
— Awakening is said of the righteous, as in “Awake and sing, dwellers in the dust,” because death is only like sleep.
וּמִזֶּה הַלָּשׁוֹן בְּדִבְרֵי רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עַל הַמִּיתָה כַּד דְּמַךְ.
— Hence our Sages’ expression for death, “when he slept.”
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם מָצִינוּ זֶה הַלָּשׁוֹן (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סה) בַּהֲדָא סִיעָא דְּפָרִיצִין וְכוּלֵי חַד מִנְּהוֹן דְּמַךְ וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ מִזֶּה כְּבָר.
— Nevertheless, we also find this expression (Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 65) concerning “that band of lawless men,” and so forth: “one of them slept,” as we have already discussed.

וְעַל זֶה גָּמַר אוֹמֵר וַיְהִי יְמֵי יַעֲקֹב שְׁנֵי חַיָּיו בִּכְלָל קמ״ז שָׁנָה שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַי״ז שָׁנָה שֶׁבַּסּוֹף נִתְבָּרְרוּ כָּל בְּחִינוֹת חַיֵּי יַעֲקֹב שֶׁהֵמָּה הַנְּפָשׁוֹת הַשְּׁפָלִים לְטוֹבָה.

— Scripture therefore concludes, “The days of Jacob, the years of his life,” totaled one hundred and forty-seven years: through the final seventeen years, all aspects of Jacob’s life, corresponding to the lowly souls, were refined for good.
כִּי עִיקַּר הַמְכוּוָּן מִן הָאָדָם רַק מַה שֶּׁיִּתְבָּרֵר בְּסוֹפוֹ
— For a person’s principal purpose is the refinement achieved at his end;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְקַן וְנִשְׁלַם כָּל מַה שֶּׁעָבַר עָלָיו
— through this, all that befell him is rectified and perfected,
דְּלֵית נְהוֹרָא אֶלָּא הַהוּא דְּנָפִיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קפד א)
— for “there is no light except that which emerges from darkness” (Zohar II 184a).
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְנוּ בְּשֵׁם הָרַב הַקָּדוֹשׁ מִפְּרְשִׁיסְחָא זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה עַל פָּסוּק וַתֵּלֶךְ לִדְרוֹשׁ אֶת הַשֵּׁם שֶׁפֵּרֵשׁ רַבִּי שְׁלֹמֹה יִצְחָקִי מַה תְּהֵא בְּסוֹפָהּ
— As we heard in the name of the holy Rabbi of Przysucha, of righteous memory, concerning “She went to inquire of Hashem,” on which Rashi explains, “What would be at her end?”
דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁרִּבְקָה חָשְׁבָה שֶׁהוּא עוּבָּר אֶחָד שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שִׁינּוּי עִתִּים וּרְצוֹנוֹת פְּעָמִים לְטוֹב וּפְעָמִים לְהֵיפֶךְ
— Rebecca thought she carried one fetus whose moods and desires varied, sometimes toward good and sometimes toward its opposite:
כִּי כְּשֶׁעוֹבֶרֶת עַל בָּתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת מְפַרְכֵּס לָצֵאת וּכְמוֹ כֵן בְּהֵיפֶךְ.
— when she passed study halls it struggled to emerge, and likewise in the opposite case.
וְעַל זֶה דָּרְשָׁה אֶת הַשֵּׁם לֵידַע אִם עַל כָּל פָּנִים יִתְבָּרֵר בַּסּוֹף לְטוֹב יִהְיֶה הַכֹּל טוֹב.
— She therefore inquired of Hashem to know whether, at least, its end would be refined for good; then everything would be good.

p: וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (ריו ב) שֶׁפָּרָשָׁה זוֹ סְתוּמָה דְּלָא אִתְחֲזֵי לְאַפְרָשָׁא בֵּין וַיֵּשֶׁב יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם בְּאֶרֶץ גֹּשֶׁן וַיֵּאָחֲזוּ בָהּ וַיִּפְרוּ וַיִּרְבּוּ מְאֹד וּבֵין וַיְחִי יַעֲקֹב

— The holy Zohar (216b) teaches that this portion is closed because no separation should appear between “Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen, and they took hold in it and were fruitful and multiplied greatly” and “Jacob lived.”
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי עִנְיַן הַפְסָקוֹת הַפָּרָשִׁיּוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה אָמְרוּ (רֵישׁ תּוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים) שֶׁהוּא כְּדֵי לִיתֵּן רֶיוַח לְמֹשֶׁה לְהִתְבּוֹנֵן בֵּין פָּרָשָׁה לְפָרָשָׁה
— The breaks between Torah sections, the Sages explain (at the beginning of Torat Kohanim), give Moses space to reflect between sections.
וּמַה שֶּׁהַפָּרָשָׁה סְתוּמָה יוֹרֶה שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ רֶיוַח לְהִתְבּוֹנֵן
— The closed portion indicates that there is no space for such reflection:
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵין שֵׂכֶל הָאֱנוֹשִׁיִּי מַשִּׂיג זֹאת עַל פִּי בִּינַת הַלֵּב מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר וַיֵּשֶׁב יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם.
— human reason, through the heart’s understanding, cannot comprehend the meaning of “Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt.”

כַּיָּדוּעַ שֶׁמִּתְּחִלָּה לֹא יָרְדוּ לְמִצְרַיִם לְהִשְׁתַּקֵּעַ בָּהּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם רַק לָגוּר בָּהּ וְעִם כָּל זֶה וַיֵּאָחֲזוּ בָהּ שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ נֶאֱחָזִים וְנִקְלָטִים בִּקְלִיפַּת מִצְרַיִם עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ כְּעוּבָּר בִּמְעֵי אִמּוֹ.

— As is known, they originally descended to Egypt to sojourn there, not, Heaven forbid, to settle permanently. Nevertheless, “they took hold in it”: they became attached and absorbed within Egypt’s impure husk, the nakedness of the land, like a fetus in its mother’s womb.

וּמִזֶּה דַּיְיקָא וַיִּפְרוּ וַיִּרְבּוּ מְאֹד שֶׁפָּרָה וְרָבָה הַקְּדוּשָּׁה וַיְחִי יַעֲקֹב בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם י״ז שָׁנָה וְהַיְינוּ שְׁלֵימוּת חַיּוּת דִּקְדוּשָּׁה לִבְחִינַת יַעֲקֹב גַּם לַנְּפָשׁוֹת הַנְּמוּכִים שֶׁיָּרְדוּ בְּתַחְתִּית הַמַּדְרֵגָה כִּי לֵית נְהוֹרָא אֶלָּא הַהוּא דְּנָפִיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא.

— Precisely from this came “they were fruitful and multiplied greatly”: holiness grew and multiplied. “Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years” means the perfected vitality of holiness for the aspect of Jacob, even for lowly souls that descended to the lowest level, for there is no light except that which emerges from darkness.
וְהוּא עִנְיַן סְתִימַת הַפָּרָשָׁה הַנְהָגַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת הָאָדָם.
— This is the significance of the closed portion: Hashem’s governance transcends human comprehension.

וְיָדוּעַ שֶׁגָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם הָיָה הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ לְכָל הַגָּלֻיּוֹת וּבָזֶה נַעֲשָׂה הָרְשִׁימָה לְדוֹרוֹת לְכָל הַגָּלֻיּוֹת וְכָל הַיְּרִידוֹת שֶׁיַּעַבְרוּ עַל נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּכְלָל וּבִפְרָט.

— It is known that the Egyptian exile was the root of all exiles. It impressed upon subsequent generations a pattern for every exile and every descent that would befall the souls of Israel, collectively and individually.
שֶׁדַּיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי הַשִּׁפְלוּת וְהַיְּרִידָה יִתְעַלֶּה הַקְּדוּשָּׁה בְּתַכְלִית לְהִתְבָּרֵר בִּשְׁלֵימוּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְחָשַׁב מַחֲשָׁבוֹת לְבִלְתִּי יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח.
— Precisely through lowliness and descent, holiness would rise to its utmost height and become completely refined, as it says, “He devises plans so that no outcast should remain cast away from Him.”

h: Joseph and the Holiness of the Covenant

p: וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז גַּם כֵּן בְּסִיּוּם הַפָּרָשָׁה וַיַּחַנְטוּ אוֹתוֹ וַיִּישֶׂם בָּאָרוֹן בְּמִצְרָיִם וּבָזֶה נִשְׁלַם סֵפֶר בְּרֵאשִׁית.
— This is also alluded to at the portion’s conclusion: “They embalmed him, and he was placed in a coffin in Egypt.” With this the Book of Genesis is completed.
שֶׁהוּא עִנְיַן שְׁלֵימוּת הַבְּרִיאָה כַּאֲשֶׁר נִשְׁלַם קְדוּשַּׁת הַבְּרִית בִּשְׁלֵימוּת.
— This signifies creation’s perfection, when the holiness of the covenant is brought to completion.
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן דַּיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי נְהוֹרָא דְּנָפִיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בִּגְמַר הַבְּרִיאָה בַּיּוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶגֶד יְסוֹד.
— This too occurs specifically through light emerging from darkness, as at creation’s completion on the sixth day, which corresponds to Yesod.
וְהָיָה מַה שֶּׁהָיָה וּבְסוֹף הַיּוֹם נֶאֱמַר וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה וְהִנֵּה טוֹב מְאֹד דַּיְיקָא שֶׁהַכֹּל נִתְקַן שֶׁיִּהְיֶה טוֹב מְאֹד.
— What happened happened, yet at the day’s end it is said, “God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good”—specifically “very,” for everything was rectified to become very good.
וּכְמוֹ כֵן נֶאֱמַר כָּאן בְּסוֹף הַסֵּפֶר עַל בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף שֶׁנִּשְׁלַם עַל יְדֵי וַיִּישֶׂם בָּאָרוֹן וְזֶה בְּמִצְרַיִם דַּיְיקָא.
— Likewise, at this book’s conclusion, Joseph’s aspect is perfected through “he was placed in a coffin”—specifically in Egypt.

וְעִנְיַן אָרוֹן הוּא שְׁלֵימוּת קְדוּשַּׁת הַבְּרִית כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ) דְּלָא עָיֵיל בַּאֲרוֹנָא אֶלָּא צַדִּיק דְּנָטִיר בְּרִית וַאֲרוֹן הַתּוֹרָה אֲרוֹן הַבְּרִית אִקְרֵי.

— The coffin signifies perfected covenantal holiness, as the holy Zohar teaches (at this portion’s end): only a righteous person who guards the covenant enters the coffin; the ark of the Torah is called the Ark of the Covenant.
וְהַיְינוּ בְּחִינַת הַטַּעַם וְהָרֵיחַ שֶׁל כֹּחַ הַתּוֹרָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ל) שֶׁהוּא עִנְיַן הִזְדַּכְּכוּת בִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַבְּרִית.
— This is the aspect of taste and fragrance, corresponding to the power of Torah and good deeds (as stated in Vayikra Rabbah, chapter 30), expressing refinement in the holiness of the covenant.
וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז תֵּיבַת וַיִּישֶׂם בָּאָרוֹן בִּשְׁנֵי יוּדִי״ן יוּ״ד תַּתָּאָה מְרַמֵּז עַל בְּחִינַת יְסוֹד שֶׁהוּא קְדוּשַּׁת הַבְּרִית בְּפֹעַל.
— This is alluded to by the word vayisem, “he was placed,” in “he was placed in a coffin,” written with two yuds: the lower yud alludes to Yesod, the holiness of the covenant in actual practice.
וְיוּ״ד עִלָּאָה הוּא בְּחִינַת חָכְמָה שֶׁהוּא טַעֲמֵי תוֹרָה.
— The upper yud is the aspect of Chokhmah, wisdom, corresponding to the Torah’s inner reasons and savor.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְנוּ הָרֶמֶז עַל זֶה מֵהָרַב הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּסַמְמָנֵי הַקְּטוֹרֶת קִנָּמוֹן תִּשְׁעָה הָרֶמֶז עַל קְדוּשַּׁת הַבְּרִית שֶׁיּוּצְרַךְ הָאָדָם לְהִתְעַצֵּם בָּזֶה מִצַּד עִקְּשׁוּת לְמַעְלָה מִן הַדַּעַת וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת תִּשְׁעָה.

— As we heard from the holy Rabbi, of righteous and holy memory, regarding the incense ingredients, “cinnamon, nine”: this alludes to covenantal holiness, in which a person must strengthen himself with a resoluteness transcending reason, through the aspect of nine.
וְהַיְינוּ מִדָּה הַתְּשִׁיעִית מֵעֶשֶׂר סְפִירוֹת מֵעֵילָא לְתַתָּא וְהוּא יְסוֹד.
— This means the ninth attribute among the ten sefirot when counted from above downward: Yesod.
וְגַם מִדָּה הַתְּשִׁיעִית מִתַּתָּא לְעֵילָא וְהוּא חָכְמָה.
— It also means the ninth attribute counted from below upward: Chokhmah.

וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר שֶׁהוּא עַל פִּי רֶמֶז הַמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מו) עַל מִילַת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דַּיְיקָא קוֹדֶם לֵידַת יִצְחָק שֶׁהוּא הַנִּימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה תְּחִלָּה וְהַיְינוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַמְקוּדָּשׁ בִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַבְּרִית בְּתוֹלָדָה.

— We may explain this through the Midrash’s allusion (Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 46) concerning our patriarch Abraham’s circumcision specifically before Isaac’s birth. Isaac was the first circumcised at eight days, embodying a root consecrated in covenantal holiness from birth.
אִיתָא שָׁם הַלָּשׁוֹן קִנָּמוֹן אֲנִי מַעֲמִיד בָּעוֹלָם וְכוּלֵי.
— The expression there is, “I establish cinnamon in the world,” and so forth.
וְהָרֶמֶז בְּמִסְפַּר תִּשְׁעָה מֵעֵילָא לְתַתָּא וּמִתַּתָּא לְעֵילָא הוּא שֶׁגַּם אִם יִזְדַּכֵּךְ גּוּפוֹ בְּפוֹעַל לִהְיוֹת נִשְׁמָר בְּכָל עִנְיְנֵי שְׁמִירָה.
— The allusion in the number nine, from above downward and from below upward, is that even if a person’s body is actually refined and guarded in every matter requiring vigilance,
אִם לֹא יִתְנַהֵג עַל פִּי כֹּחַ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁקֶר עָנָה בְנַפְשׁוֹ.
— if he does not conduct himself according to the Torah’s power, he has testified falsely against his own soul.
רַק דַּיְיקָא שֶׁיִּהְיוּ שְׁנֵי הַבְּחִינוֹת כְּאֶחָד שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית עַל פִּי כֹּחַ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת הַטַּעַם וְהָרֵיחַ וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה וַיִּישֶׂם בָּאָרוֹן בְּמִצְרָיִם דַּיְיקָא:

— Rather, the two aspects must specifically unite: guarding the covenant through the Torah’s power, corresponding to taste and fragrance. Through this, “he was placed in a coffin,” specifically in Egypt.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, end of Vayechi: “We learned: Why are there two letters yod in “vayyisem”? Joseph guarded the covenant below and guarded the covenant above. When he departed from the world, he was placed in two arks: an ark below and an ark above. What is the ark above? As it says: “Behold the Ark of the Covenant of the Master of all the earth.” The ark above is called the Ark of the Covenant, for none inherits it except one who guards the covenant. Because Joseph guarded the covenant, he was placed in two arks.”

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 46:2: ““There is a time for everything, and a season for every purpose under heaven.” Abraham had a time when circumcision was given to him, as it says: “On that very day Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised.” His children had a time when they were circumcised twice, once in Egypt and once in the wilderness, as it says: “All the people who came out were circumcised.” Why was Abraham not circumcised at forty-eight, when he recognized his Creator? So as not to close the door before converts. Should you say that he ought to have been circumcised at eighty-five, when God spoke with him at the covenant between the pieces? Rather, it was so that Isaac would come from a holy drop. Why not at eighty-six, when Ishmael was born? Reish Lakish said: “I am establishing cinnamon in the world.” Just as cinnamon bears fruit whenever you fertilize and hoe it, so Abraham’s blood had become thick, his impulse had ceased, his desire had ceased, and his blood had become bound up. He said: If circumcision is so beloved, why was it not given to Adam?”
